digest.component_or_area: snapshot janitor / root disk pressure mitigation
propositions: The snapshot janitor's reclaim trigger uses an absolute 2 GiB free-space floor that is disk-size-blind, crossing only at 93.3% used on a 30 GiB volume—above the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% observed peak
The 7-day cold-trim grace window exceeds the container's actual lifetime (recreated hourly), rendering it dead code and leaving the space watermark as the sole active reclaim trigger

The janitor correctly evicts nothing when its triggers are unreachable; the failure is structural, not operational—proved by runtime injection of free-space values showing 0 evictions at 85% and 90% used, first eviction only past 93.3%

Review-bot snapshots materialize ~620 MiB per review keyed on tickets ref that advances every ~26 seconds with minimal file deltas, producing 2.5–10 GiB/h growth that outpaces any reclaim the current watermark allows

Adding a volume-relative headroom term (free_watermark_pct as whole percent) makes the reclaim trigger engage before the alarm floor by taking the maximum of absolute and relative thresholds, with hysteresis via RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT ensuring overshoot rather than re-firing

The fix restores the documented defense ordering (runbook: janitor reclaims first, alarm is the backstop) on small volumes where the absolute floor becomes reachable before the operator's alarm threshold
